defect.evidence_quote: [a]s to what is to be taken, nothing is left to the discretion of the officer executing the warrant.
defect.problem: The black-letter callout is broadly supported in substance, but as framed it contains verbatim quote and pincite claims that are not character-verifiable from the disclosed evidence. The Steele quoted phrase does not appear in the disclosed Steele pinpoints, and the Stanford pinpoint quote differs from the page's quoted fragment. Groh also should be narrowed to unincorporated supporting papers/documents because the disclosed evidence stresses that no document was incorporated by reference.
defect.proposed_fix: Add full text files or corrected pinpoints for Steele, Stanford, and Groh; quote Stanford as the lake pinpoint states; remove quotation marks around the Steele formulation unless the exact opinion text is disclosed; narrow Groh to non-incorporated supporting documents or documents not made part of the warrant.

reasons: Steele treatment supports the place rule generally, but Steele pinpoints pin-503 and pin-503b do not contain the quoted words "can with reasonable effort ascertain and identify the place intended."

Stanford pin-485b gives the fuller text "[a]s to what is to be taken, nothing is left to the discretion of the officer executing the warrant," not the page's quoted "nothing . . . to the discretion of the officer executing the warrant."
Groh pin-557 supports the warrant-itself rule but includes the limiting fact that "no document was incorporated by reference," which the callout does not state.
residual_risks: No text/*.txt files were disclosed, so exact quote-fidelity and page-pincite landing cannot be independently verified beyond lake pinpoints and judgment fields.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: State the rule with exact lake-supported language and reserve quotation marks for text present in pinpoints or disclosed opinion text.
